title: AsyncDIMM: Achieving Asynchronous Execution in DIMM-Based Near-Memory Processing
problem: DIMM-based near-memory processing (NMP) architectures cannot efficiently support asynchronous execution between host CPUs and near-memory accelerators (NMAs) because independent memory controllers on both sides cause memory bus contention and potential DRAM errors when issuing concurrent accesses. Existing designs resort to synchronous execution, wasting either host or NMA compute.
motivation: The memory wall makes near-memory processing attractive for bandwidth-bound workloads, but synchronous host-NMA execution severely underutilizes hardware by idling one side while the other accesses DRAM.
method: AsyncDIMM introduces three operational modes on existing memory buses: single access (host or NMA only), concurrent access, and seamless mode switching. An offload-schedule-return mechanism with explicit and implicit synchronization ensures correct memory access semantics across modes. Optimized timing constraints reduce offload latency; a locality-aware switch-recovery method minimizes mode-switch overhead; adaptive batching with timing-division multiplexing notifications improves return bandwidth. Hardware modifications are limited to conventional host and NMA memory controllers and validated on FPGA.
key_novelty: Offload-schedule-return mechanism with dual synchronization modes (explicit and implicit) enabling correct concurrent host+NMA DRAM access on existing unmodified memory buses without protocol changes.
contributions: Identification of memory bus contention and DRAM state races as the fundamental barriers to asynchronous DIMM-NMP execution.
AsyncDIMM: single/concurrent/hybrid access modes with offload-schedule-return synchronization for correct concurrent host+NMA memory access.
Optimized timing constraints, locality-aware switch-recovery, and adaptive batch with TDM notifications to maximize bandwidth and minimize latency.
1.19x-1.92x speedup over four NMP baselines; up to 2.25x bandwidth utilization; 47% access latency reduction; FPGA-validated.

metrics.other: Up to 2.25x bandwidth utilization uplift; 47% access latency reduction

baselines: Four DIMM-NMP baseline configurations with synchronous execution
limitations: Hardware modifications to memory controllers are required on both host and NMA sides; evaluation is on FPGA emulation rather than real DIMM-NMP silicon.
primary_theme: Asynchronous host-NMA co-execution in DIMM-based near-memory processing
